Help

Overview

The graph explorer shows the state of an AGNOS project at one commit, as agnos-graph wrote it: every element (features, requirements, ADRs, decisions, plans, tasks), the sections of their documents, the scanned source files, and, when the graph was built with them, the functions and the history.

It shows the state and judges nothing: coverage, findings and scores are the performance center's.

  • Menus: File opens a graph file, saves and opens views, and imports or exports the saved queries and views; View chooses the view; Filter clears the query or shows every node; Help opens this guide.
  • Panels: the facets on the left, the view in the middle, the selected node's detail on the right. Drag their edges, or use the arrow keys on them, to resize.
  • Saved views: File, Save view… keeps under a name the tab, the query, the facets, the hidden and isolated nodes, the period, the 3D dimensions, layout and projection, and the relation colours; the view's name in the File menu restores them all. The views are kept in this browser: File, Export views… saves them to a JSON file, Import views… reads them back. Both exports open a save dialog that remembers its last folder, in browsers that offer one; elsewhere the file is downloaded.
  • Image: on Graph 2D or Graph 3D, File, Export image saves the view as a PNG image of its size, the 3D labels included, through the same save dialog.
  • Another graph: drop an agnos-graph.json file on the page, or choose File, Open graph file.

Graph

Every shown node and relation, coloured by type and by relation kind, as the legend at the bottom says.

  • Move: drag a node; it keeps its place when the filters change. Drag the background to pan, use the wheel or the + and − buttons to zoom, Fit to see every shown node.
  • Layout: type columns, grid, circle, concentric, tree or force-directed, left to right or top to bottom where the layout has a direction.
  • Right-click a node to select it, hide it or show only its neighbours at 1, 2 or 3 hops; the background to choose a layout.
  • Hover a node to read its properties without changing the selection.
  • Graph 3D: the View menu chooses the cylindrical layout (height, angle around the axis, radius) or the cartesian one (x by the angle, y by the height, z by the radius, on three graduated axes it shows or hides); the axis indicator of the bottom left corner names what each direction shows.

Nodes

One row per shown node: ID, type, trigram, status, title, location, and its incoming and outgoing relation counts.

Click a header to sort, again to reverse; drag a header's right edge to resize its column. Click a row, or press Enter on it, to show the node in the detail panel.

Relations

One row per shown relation: its source and target, its kind (contains, refs, code, call), the link field it was declared in (Requirement refs, Dependencies…, or text for a mention), the line and the proof text.

Sort and resize the columns as in the node table.

Facets and queries

Every filter applies to every view at once.

  • Facets: uncheck a type, trigram, status, relation kind or link field to hide its nodes or relations; All and None check or uncheck a whole facet.
  • Query: space-separated terms, all met: key:value, key:a,b, key:!value, key:~text, cites:TYPE[field], cited-by:TYPE[field], each negated by a leading !; a query starting with edge selects relations by kind, field, from and to. Clicking a facet value while the query field has the focus writes its term.
  • Saved queries: + Save query keeps the current query as a button; Edit buttons renames, moves or deletes them. File exports and imports them as a JSON file.
  • Selection: the detail panel hides the selected node, isolates its neighbourhood and widens it by one hop; hidden nodes are listed above the view, a click shows them again.

Time

When the graph was built with --history, each node is dated by its first commit in the history read: the first commit that changed its document lines, its file or its function. A node no commit of the history changed is dated the history's first commit.

  • Period: drag the two handles of the time bar to choose the first and the last day; every view shows only the nodes dated in the period, and the relations between them.
  • Time menu: Whole history, Last 7 days and Last 30 days set the period at once.
  • Playback: Play moves a cursor from the period's first day to its last, at the chosen speed in days per second: the views show the nodes dated up to the cursor, so the graph grows before your eyes. Pause keeps the cursor where it is; Stop shows the whole period again. With Loop checked, the playback starts again from the first day, until it is paused or stopped.
  • Mode: Cumulative shows every node since the period's first day; Last 7 days and Last 30 days show only the nodes dated in those days before the cursor, to see where the work moves.

The graph is the state at one commit: the period shows when today's nodes first appeared, not what was removed before. Without --history, the time bar is hidden and the Time menu is disabled.

Appearance

Each relation kind has a colour, drawn in the graph and in its legend. To bring a kind forward, choose Appearance, Colour of <kind>…, or click the kind in the legend, then pick a colour.

The colours are kept in this browser. Appearance, Reset colours gives every kind its default colour again. The node types keep their colours.
